title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 5.69 (versions follow prime numbers; 569 after 563): her installer, and her independence. In the folder instalador/, instalar-luma.exe asks where, makes her folders, assembles her there with her own assembler (PDP, from its seed, running on her kernel: what it builds is the same, byte for byte, as the project's build), puts her knowledge in her house and leaves two shortcuts on the desktop. luma.exe wakes her (in front, as big as the screen), keeps her one, and lets her be born again when she decides to sleep: Git Bash and PowerShell are no longer needed to run her. No path is written down: everything is found from where luma.exe is. The two programs that speak to Windows are assembled with flat assembler (FASM) by Tomasz Grysztar, as the kernel. Also: a borrowed answer no longer brings the name of who was spoken to. Not tested on another computer yet. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v5.57: Luma purificada. Prototipo de investigación.
